title: benjamin-ross-sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-26
content:
On-call notes - Benjamin Ross - 2026-03-26

Summary:
- Major PagerDuty page at 02:14 UTC: high CPU across model-serving-prod region (us-west-2). Impact: increased latency for hosted API text-generation endpoints (~90th p50->p95 spike), several customer errors reported.
- Immediate mitigation: rolled back autoscaler change from earlier deploy, increased dedicated pool capacity, restarted gateway pods for affected nodes. Latency returned to baseline by 02:48 UTC.

Incidents / Timeline:
- 02:08 UTC - small number of 5xx errors start appearing; alerting thresholds hit for 5xx rate on /v1/generate (prometheus alert SRE-5xx-rate).
- 02:14 UTC - PagerDuty page triggered: high CPU across runtime-gateway hosts (cpu_util > 90% sustained). Multiple hosts reporting heavy steal time and long GC pauses in runtime process.
- 02:20 UTC - Took initial triage: inspected grafana dashboard (model-serving-overview), confirmed autoscaler had recently rolled out change (rolling update at 01:50 UTC, PR #1284).
- 02:23 UTC - Scoped root cause hypothesis: autoscaler bug causing many short-lived replicas to be created and killed rapidly (thundering herd), leading to contention on NVMe / cache warmup with heavy disk I/O and CPU overhead.
- 02:30 UTC - Mitigation plan: revert autoscaler change -> roll back to previous autoscaler image (deployed by me 02:32 UTC). Meanwhile increased dedicated GPU pool by +3 instances to absorb traffic.
- 02:40 UTC - Restarted gateway pods on two noisy hosts (graceful restart) to clear stuck processes; removed those nodes from LB while draining.
- 02:48 UTC - Metrics normalized: CPU down to 45-60% on hosts, 5xx rate back to baseline. Customer-reported errors decreased.
- 03:05 UTC - Post-incident checks: validated KV cache hit rates, confirmed no residual OOMs.

Pages and alerts:
- PagerDuty incident: PD-23177
- Alerts fired: SRE-CPU-high (multiple hosts), SRE-5xx-rate, SRE-autoscaler-failure

Immediate actions (done):
- Rolled back autoscaler image to previous stable (PR rollback, revert commit applied). Owner: Benjamin Ross (me).
- Increased dedicated pool capacity for us-west-2 (+3 GPU instances) to lower pressure. Owner: infra-autoscale (automation) triggered by me.
- Drained and restarted 2 gateway pods on host i-0a1b2c3d; verified restarts succeed.
- Notified affected customers via #customer-notify with status update and ETA for follow-ups.

Follow-ups / TODOs (triage items):
- SRE-443 (Jira): Autoscaler regression root cause + fix. Steps:
  - Add reproducible test that simulates high short-lived traffic and validates autoscaler behavior. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-04-02.
  - Add rate limit on replica creation (circuit breaker) to autoscaler. Owner: Platform Eng (TBD). Due: 2026-04-09.
  - Improve autoscaler healthchecks to avoid thundering herd scenario. Owner: Lena G. Due: 2026-04-05.
- Update runbook: "model-serving high CPU" to include explicit rollback steps for autoscaler and steps to scale dedicated pool. Owner: Benjamin Ross. Due: 2026-03-30.
- Post-incident blameless postmortem doc: create Confluence page using incident template. Owner: Benjamin Ross + Maya. Due: 2026-03-29.
- Add dashboard panels for NVMe I/O and process-level GC pauses that triggered this event. Owner: Observability team. Due: 2026-03-31.

Runbook notes / gaps spotted:
- Current runbook notes the autoscaler rollback but doesn't document how to increase dedicated pool quickly (had to run manual infra CLI). Add exact CLI command and required permissions.
- No playbook for detecting cache warmup thundering herd; need to add guidance: detect rapid replica churn + NVMe I/O spike -> pause autoscaler + scale pool.
- Alert thresholds: SRE-CPU-high uses host-level CPU > 85% for 5m; during this event the problem started at 60-75% on hosts but process-level CPU and I/O spiking. Need finer-grained process-level alerting.

Customer comms:
- Draft sent in #customer-notify: short summary + root-cause hypothesis + next steps. Will convert to formal status update after postmortem.

Notes to self (personal):
- Remember to add the explicit rollback command to runbook before handing off to next oncall.
- Follow up with Platform Eng about adding a "slow-start" on replica creation (backoff) to reduce cache warmup pressure.
- Check if the autoscaler PR #1284 had a test for burst traffic (looks like it did not).

Small checklist (quick):
- [x] Acknowledged pagerduty and triaged
- [x] Rolled back autoscaler change
- [x] Scaled dedicated pool -> normalized
- [ ] Update runbook (assigned)
- [ ] Create Confluence postmortem (assigned)
- [ ] Add autoscaler regression test (assigned)

Links / refs used during triage:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/model-serving-overview
- PR that rolled autoscaler change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1284
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-443
- PD incident: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-23177

Misc / stray thoughts:
- Consider adding an automated canary for autoscaler changes that runs a short-lived load test in a staging pool. Could catch this type of regression earlier.
- If we introduce a circuit-breaker/backoff for replica creation, ensure it interacts well with bursty legitimate traffic (e.g., batch job startup).

End of notes.
